question: Should ClawHub broadly exclude crypto, blockchain, finance, and trading content from the public registry, or retain behavior-based moderation with narrower prohibited conduct?
rationale: Current main implements contextual security and moderation rules, while this RFC explicitly leaves category scope and enforcement effects unresolved; source inspection cannot safely choose that marketplace-policy boundary.

options.title: Keep behavior-based policy
options.body: Allow legitimate financial and on-chain tools while prohibiting deceptive, unsafe, spammy, or malicious conduct and escalating high-risk releases to review.

options.title: Ban broad categories
options.body: Exclude crypto, blockchain, finance, and trading packages from the public registry regardless of their narrower purpose or safeguards.

options.title: Default-deny with exceptions
options.body: Permit documented read-only, educational, identity, registry, or reputation cases only after human review.

recommendation.title: Keep behavior-based policy
recommendation.body: Allow legitimate financial and on-chain tools while prohibiting deceptive, unsafe, spammy, or malicious conduct and escalating high-risk releases to review.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen authored this RFC and the recent acceptable-usage clarification and has the strongest current history in the affected moderation paths.
